Commentary.Commentary: Mignon du Preez remained not out till the end and added some crucial stands with Dane van Niekerk and Chloe Tryon in the end. English bowlers apart from Natalie Sciver and Jenny Gunn were very economical. Anya Shrubsole was outstanding finishing with 1/33. The fielding, however, was not up to the mark and they conceded a few extra runs. Target of 219 seems to be very gettable especially with the batting line-up that England possess. The Proteas though have a superb bowling attack and can create an upset. Join us soon for an interesting chase.

An unbeaten 48-run stand in the end has helped South Africa to get to a fighting total. After losing the dangerous Liselle Lee early in the innings, they lost Trisha Chetty soon as well. However, Laura Wolvaardt and Mignon du Preez steadied the ship and added 77 runs for the third wicket. Both the batsmen went on to register half centuries as well. Once again they lost a couple of quick wickets and were pushed on the back foot.

Full and outside off, driven straight to cover. Initially, there is no run but the fielder returns a wild throw to the bowler who is unable to collect and concedes an overthrow. A sloppy way to finish. South Africa finish on 218/6!
Outside off, played straight to point.

Now the substitute injures herself almost! A replica of the previous delivery. Full and outside off, Luus powers this down the ground. Danielle Wyatt comes across from long on and dives and seems to be a bit uncomfortable. Another two runs taken. Seems to be okay. Meanwhile, Shrubsole is limping off into the dressing room.
Anya Shrubsole is off the field after she damaged her ankle while stopping the previous ball. Danielle Wyatt replaces her.

Full on middle, chipped over  the bowler. Does not have enough on it to bisect the field and long on and long off get across. However, Anya Shrubsole from long on slips on her ankle while diving and is in pain. Two runs taken.
Now du Preez walks across and this time Gunn bowls it straighter. Another sweep for a run.
Walks across her stumps and Gunn bowls it outside leg. Swept behind square leg for a single.
JENNY GUNN to bowl the last over.

Around off, worked through mid-wicket. Should have been just a single but a fumble from Fran Wilson converted it into a couple. Brunt is not happy, yelling out her frustration to Wilson. 8 from the over and Brunt finishes with figures of 10-1-40-0.

FOUR! Finally a boundary for the Proteas. Backs away to the leg side, exposing all the stumps, then reaches out and drives this aerially over covers for a boundary. Moves to 73 from 93 balls with 5 boundaries.
Full and straight, flicked to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Another dot! Full and outside off, heaved straight to mid on. du Preez wants a single but is sent back.
Short and outside off, Luus looks to cut but the slowness of the ball on this already sluggish surface induces a bottom edge.
On middle and leg, flicked through square leg for a single.

Short and outside off, pulled down to long on for one more. End of a good day's work for Shrubsole - 10-1-33-1. Gets a warm round of applause from the crowd. Could not get too many wickets but built up the pressure nicely.

Delivered from the back of the hand, a slower ball, Luus looks to punch it through the off side but gets a thick inside edge which races through fine leg. However, Laura Marsh does well from short fine leg to keep the batters to a single.
Another long hop, pulled to deep mid-wicket again for one.
A short ball now, outside off, heaved to mid-wicket in the deep for a run. 200 UP FOR SOUTH AFRICA. 15 balls left. How much can they get?
That is lucky for the bowler. Fine leg is inside the circle and Shrubsole bowls it outside leg. Luus paddles it but straight to short fine leg! Not even a single. A gold-dust dot ball.
Banged in short, pulled straight to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Short, pulled through mid-wicket for only one. Terrific over. Just 3 from it.
Stands well outside leg, aiming to go inside out. There is no one placed in the deep on the off side, hence that stance. But the ball is very full, on the stumps and it can only be pushed to cover.
Down the leg side, MdP misses her flick and is hit on the pads. A mild LBW appeal ensues but one could see all the three stumps.
This foxes the batter, change of pace, outside off, Mignon looks to punch it through the off side but misses.

Faster delivery in line of the stumps, pushed towards long on for a run. Very good in these death overs, is Katherine Brunt. Have not seen her taking too many wickets in this phase but has not given away too many runs either.
Down the leg side, flicked through square leg for a single.
Another bowling change. KATHERINE BRUNT is back on.
A dot to finish. Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Full and straight, worked towards long on but Natalie Sciver dives to her left from short mid-wicket and stops the ball.
Shows all her stumps, getting well across and bunts a very full ball outside off to long on for a single.
Another short ball, outside off, slower in pace, du Preez goes back and heaves it over mid-wicket. However, Jenny Gunn stationed at widish long on gets to it and keeps the batsmen to a couple.
Drops it a bit short, Luus swivels and pulls it behind square leg for a single.
Very straight from Shrubsole, pushed towards long on but the bowler herself intervenes.
ANYA SHRUBSOLE is back on.
Full on middle and off, pushed down to long on for a single. A good over for South Africa, 12 from it.
Full and outside off, worked through mid-wicket for one more.
Very full outside off, worked towards long on for a run.
MISFIELD, FOUR! Gunn is not happy. Full and outside off, Luus strikes it back. Gunn tries to stop it with her left foot but cannot. Mid off gets around but dives over the ball and it goes through.
A slower ball now, on middle, worked towards long on for a single. There is a misfield and they think about the second but then let it be.
FOUR! HAMMERED! Short ball, outside off, du Preez rocks back and pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary! There was a fielder in the deep but the ball raced away too quickly.
Comes down the track and drives it to long off for a single.
This is wide outside off, Mignon backs away and looks to drive but gets a thickish outside edge past short third man. Two runs taken.
Tossed up outside off, driven straight to short extra cover.
Another sweep shot played, just a run.
Down the leg side, du Preez goes back and works it towards fine leg for a run.
Full and outside off, swept to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
The batsman has driven it straight down the ground.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
12th ODI Fifty for du Preez but her first against England.
Outside off, pushed through the covers for a run. A very good innings from du Preez.
Outside off, Luus looks to run it down to third man but gets a thick outside edge. A single results.
SUNE LUUS strides out to bat.

OUT! Soft dismissal! Typical Jenny Gunn dismissal. Full and around off, taking the pace off the ball, Tryon does not read it and attempts to drive it to long off. However, the bat turns in her hand and she spoons a simple return catch to Gunn. South Africa losing their way here.
JENNY GUNN is brought back into the attack.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single. 4 runs and a run out from that over.
Outside off, punched off the back foot.

Full on middle, du Preez gets a bit of an edge to the leg side. This time the bowler herself gets to the ball, there is another mix-up, she looks to throw but it is a weak one as she is off balance. A single taken.
CHLOE TRYON replaces her skipper.

OUT! Van Niekerk is short! Massive blow for South Africa. They needed their captain till the finish just as she played against India the other day. Not to be today. Full on middle, du Preez flicked it towards short mid-wicket and set off a couple of steps. Van Niekerk immediately responded but then du Preez sent her back. Too late. The skipper had come a bit too far and had to dive. The throw came in to the bowler who disturbed the stumps. Replays showed the bat to be on the line and in air as well. That is the end of a 42-run stand.
The umpire has gone upstairs to check whether van Niekerk has made her ground while being sent back by her partner. Looks close!
Shorter in length, around off, spinning away, van Niekerk goes back and punches it through the covers for a run.
Tossed up wide outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
ALEX HARTLEY is back, replacing Brunt.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
SIX! Lovely hit! Flighted wide outside off, actually a good delivery, seeing the Protea skipper down the track but the captain adjusts well and smashes it over long off.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball for a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
A bit more flight outside off but on seeing van Niekerk charge out to her, Marsh slows the pace. Van Niekerk adjusts well and punches it through the covers for a run.
Tossed up outside off, driven towards sweeper cover for a single.
Brunt tails it in with pace, blocked away. 22 runs came from the Batting Powerplay. It proved to be a good one for England!
FOUR! THROUGH THE INFIELD! Length delivery outside off, Dane glides it past short third man and collects her first boundary against Katherine Brunt.
Van Niekerk makes room this time. Brunt takes the pace off the ball and surprises the opposition skipper, who defends it on the off side.
WELL KEPT, TAYLOR! Length delivery outside off, van Niekerk tries to be innovative. Goes for the reverse scoop but misses it completely. Taylor who is standing up collects it superbly.
Du Preez again walks across and flicks the fuller delivery to fine leg for a single.
Angling into the batsman, du Preez stays leg sidish and defends it in the mid-wicket region.
Full outside off, driven to covers.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Full around off, Van Niekerk desperate to up the ante, goes for the reverse sweep. Gets a top edge and the ball flies over Sarah Taylor to short fine leg. A single is taken.
Marsh expects Dane to give the charge and fires the ball in. The South African skipper yorks herself and does well to dig it out to mid-wicket.

FOUR! EDGY! Van Niekerk after playing out a maiden, decides to go after Marsh. Dances down the track and looks to play an expansive drive. Gets an outside edge and the ball swirls past the short third man fielder to the fence behind. 150 up for the Proteas!
Spinning into the pads, worked with the spin on the leg side for a single.
Yes she can! Bowls it at a good pace on a length around off, dabbed on the off side. Superb stuff from Katherine Brunt!
Leg cutter on the fuller length around off. Van Niekerk drives it straight to the man at covers. 5 dots in a row. Can she bowl a maiden in the Powerplay?
Fuller around off, blocked on the off side.
Shortish delivery outside off, Dane pulls it nicely but for the third time in a row finds the fielder at mid-wicket.
Similar delivery, this time van Niekerk sits down and slaps it in front of square but finds the fielder again.
Another crossed seam delivery outside off, cut straight to point.

DRINKS BREAK. Good passage of play for England. Heather Knight has turned out to be the woman with the golden arm, picking two wickets in one over, including the prized one of Wolvaardt. South Africa will have to get some sort of a move on, if they have to reach 250 from here. Only 10 have come in 2 overs of the Batting Powerplay so far and they will aim to maximize in the next 3 overs. This partnership will be the key.
Served around off, spinning in, driven to long on for a single.
The batsman drives the ball straight down the ground back to the bowler.
FOUR! CHEEKY! Fuller on the stumps. The SA skipper kneels down and paddle sweeps it fine down the leg side. Beats short fine leg and collects a boundary.
Tossed up outside off, spinning in. Dane looks to run it down at first but then adjusts well to the spin. Defends it off the inner half down the track.
Spinning down leg, worked behind square on the leg side for a single.
Quicker through the air outside off, spinning in, pushed in the cover region.
Shortish delivery outside off, cut to cover-point for no run.
Short delivery, angling into the batsman. Pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Pitched outside off, run down to third man for a single.
Angling into the batsman, van Niekerk is surprised a touch by the ball nipping back in. However, she does well to defend it off the inner half on the leg side.
A crossed seam delivery on a back of a length outside off. Punched through covers for a single.
Short and angling down leg, worked off the hips to fine leg. A single taken.
KATHERINE BRUNT comes back into the attack.
BATTING POWERPLAY taken! For the next 5 overs, a maximum of 3 fielders are allowed outside the circle.
Quicker delivery on a length around off, punched down to long on for a single.
Another full delivery outside off. This time Dane drives it crisply but finds the fielder at covers.
Full on the stumps, mistimed her drive back to the bowler.
Slower one, sliding into the batsman. Van Niekerk gets across and defends it on the leg side.
Full outside off, driven through covers for a single.
Slower one outside off, du Preez leans ahead and blocks it on the off side.
LAURA MARSH is back on.
Full and down the leg side, flicked away for one more.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for one.
This is quicker, fuller and straighter, driven back to the bowler.
Slowly bowled on the pads, flicked through square leg for a run.
Full and outside leg, pushed with soft hands through mid-wicket for a single. Du Preez had to dive in to make the single.
Outside off, pushed toward cover.

WIDE. Smart delivery actually. Knight slips this down the leg side, du Preez looks to flick but while doing so, gets out of her crease. Sarah Taylor is blinded, hence fumbles and concedes a bye as well.
Short of a length delivery, mistimed cut to point.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Leg cutter around off, van Niekerk is beaten on her cut again.
On a length outside off, van Niekerk looks to punch it on the off side but gets beaten.
Shortish delivery outside off, punched through covers for a single.
Fullish outside off, driven to mid off.
Shortish delivery around off, van Niekerk waits for it and then blocks. End of an eventful over - A wicket, a dropped catch and a run out!
Skipper DANE VAN NIEKERK walks in at number 6, replacing Kapp.

OUT! KAPP DEPARTS! Heather Knight is a relieved person! Fullish delivery, dabbed in the cover region. Du Preez takes off for a quick single but Kapp is a touch slow to respond. To the latter's dismay the throw is at her end and a very good one. Taylor collects the ball and takes the bails off in a flash. The umpire takes the decision upstairs and the replay shows that Kapp has to walk back.
A run out appeal! Is Kapp in trouble? The umpire has gone upstairs...
On the pads, flicked on the leg side for a single.

DROPPED! Oh dear, the batsman and the bowler both made a mess out of it. It was a juicy full toss on off by Knight, asking to be hit. One couldn't have asked for a better first delivery than this. However, her execution was miserable. She hit it straight to Heather, who got both her hands to it but failed to hold onto it.
MARIZANNE KAPP walks out to bat.

OUT! TIMBER! Bowling change works for Knight! Bowls another short delivery on middle. Wolvaardt goes back to pull but the low bounce does her in. She tries to adjust but it's too late and the ball sneaks through to shatter the woodwork. This is a big, big wicket as Woolvaardt was looking really dangerous now. Much-needed breakthrough for the home side!
Starts off with a loosener. Bowls a short delivery into the batsman. Pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Change in bowling as HEATHER KNIGHT introduces herself into the attack!
Pitched up delivery outside off, driven to sweeper cover for a single.
Short delivery, Wolvaardt slashes hard at it. Gets it off the outer half to third man for a single.
Length delivery outside off, glided to point.
Slower delivery around off, du Preez gets low and taps it in the cover region for a single.
On a length outside off, punched solidly but straight to point.
Full on middle, driven to mid off.
Around off, watchfully defended.
FOUR! Now a glorious shot to follow. Full on middle, driven straight back down the ground. This time Marsh has no chance.
FOUR! FETCH THAT! Very powerfully struck. Full on middle, Wolvaardt hammers this through mid on. Laura Marsh dives to her left, gets a finger to it but the ball races through to the fence behind.
Outside off, played straight to cover.
Full and wide outside off, eased behind point for a couple.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Just around off, watchfully defended.
Short and outside off, punched through point for a run.

Lisa Sthalekar on air mentions that these two batting together make bowlers adjust their lengths as Wolvaardt stays deep in the crease while du Preez keeps shimmying across. This is an important partnership for SA!
Landed outside off, Wolvaardt stays flat-footed and attempts the cut but misses.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Outside off, played behind point for a single.
Outside off, driven straight to cover.
On middle and leg, worked to the leg side for a single.
Short and outside off, Wolvaardt goes back and punches it back to the bowler who dives after the ball passes her down to long off. Easy run conceded.
This is down the leg side, Mignon goes back and plays it behind square leg for a single.
Very full outside off, du Preez looks to play the reverse sweep but misses.
Slightly shorter, punched towards short cover.
Slowly tossed up on middle and off, watchfully defended.
Around off, watchfully blocked out.
Very straight, would have been dead plumb had Mignon missed but she didn't and clipped it through mid-wicket for a single. Shrubsole has her hands on her head.
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
This is on the pads, clipped straight to short mid-wicket.
Outside off, punched through point where Fran Wilson does well.
FOUR! That is a cracking shot. Short and wide outside off, du Preez slaps it behind point and gets a boundary!
ANYA SHRUBSOLE comes back on.
Short and outside off, Wolvaardt misses out, cutting the ball straight to point.
Goes back and punches it through point for one.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a run.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. They pick up a single.
Short and outside off, punched off the back foot towards long off for a single. That brings up the 50-RUN STAND.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Short again, pulled towards deep mid-wicket where the fielder does well running to her left. Keeps the batters to a single.
7th ODI Fifty for Wolvaardt! 4th in this tournament. Is she in good form or what...

FOUR! Nicely hit! Slightly fuller in line of the stumps, Wolvaardt goes back and smashes it straight back over the bowler for a boundary! Not a bad time for this knock. South Africa will hope she will get a big one today.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Fires it down the leg side, flicked through square leg for a single.
A short ball outside off, du Preez looks to pull but misses and is hit on the pads.
It's been driven superbly through the covers.
Short and outside off, punched behind point for a run.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Tossed up outside off, du Preez comes down the track and drives it back to the bowler.
Outside off, punched through the off side for a run.
On middle and leg, flicked through square leg for a single.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Around off, watchfully blocked.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
This is full and wide outside off, driven through the covers for a run.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Tossed up outside off, driven back to the bowler.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
Tossed up around middle, watchfully defended.
Fuller in length, outside off, Laura leans and drives it through mid off for a single.
FOUR! That is a fine shot. Dropped short and outside off, Wolvaardt goes back and pulls it over the bowler for a boundary!
Pushes this through the covers for a single.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Driven through the covers by the batsman.
Half volley outside off, driven through the covers for one.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a quick run. The throw comes in to the bowler but she fumbles. WOLVAARDT WOULD HAVE BEEN A GONER.
A long hop first up, outside off, slapped through point for a single.
JENNY GUNN comes on to bowl now. She is a tricky customer on these slow wickets.
Straying on the pads, worked in the square leg region for a quick single. Most expensive over of the innings so far, 10 from it!
FOUR! PUNCHED AWAY! Shorter around off, spinning away. Mignon waits for it and pulls it against the spin with disdain. Gets it in the gap at mid-wicket and collects a boundary.
Full outside off, driven back to the bowler.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

FOUR! IN THE AIR, SAFE! Hartley gives it a nice loop, lands it outside off. Draws du Preez into a drive and she obliges. The ball lobs off the toe end over the extra cover fielder and wide of Brunt at covers. The latter gives it a chase but the ball beats her to the fence.
Fuller on the boots, Wolvaardt kneels down and sweeps to fine leg for a single.
Full outside off, spinning in, driven through covers for a single.
Tossed up outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Marsh gets her line wrong this time. Drags it short and down the leg side. Du Preez just helps it on its way to fine leg for a single.
Once again du Preez takes an off-stumps guard. Plays it with the spin to mid-wicket.
Mignon covers the stumps and pushes it back to the bowler.
Served outside off, the ball grips and spins in with extra bounce. Du Preez does well to dab it to point.

DRINKS BREAK. A decent hour of cricket. South Africa started well only to be pegged back by England. The visitors do not have a great history of strong batting but the good thing for them is that Laura Wolvaardt is still out there and looking fluent. The pitch looks a good one to bat on and 250 will be a minimum. England, on the other hand, have not quite been successful in trying to keep a lid on the proceedings. They have cut down the boundaries but a few attacking fields, especially to the new batter could induce more pressure and subsequently, wickets.
Wolvaardt makes room and then punches it with the spin on the off side.
Sliding into the batsman, tucked through mid-wicket for a single.

HARTLEY MAKES A MESS OF A CHANCE! Shortish delivery, spinning away. Once again Wolvaardt was done in by the ball holding a touch after pitching. She chipped it over the bowler's head. It was at a catchable height but Hartley misjudged it completely. Was late to get her hands up and the ball flew over it to long off for a single.
Shortish delivery around off, punched off the back foot to covers.
Full outside off, spinning away, pushed to mid off.
Full down the leg side, du Preez goes down on one knee and sweeps it through backward square leg for a single.
Shortish outside off, du Preez bends low and cuts it through cover-point for a single.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Spinning into the batsman, turned to mid-wicket.
Wide outside off, glided to point.

ALMOST DRAGGED ON! Quicker through the air, outside off. Wolvaardt looks to drive with hard hands against the spin. Gets an inside edge but is lucky that it deflects onto the pads and not onto the stumps.
Full outside off, spinning in, driven back to the bowler.
Again on a shorter length, mistimed punch to long off for a single.
Tossed up outside off, pushed to covers.
Fullish outside off, driven to extra cover.
IN THE AIR BUT SAFE! On a shortish length outside off. Holds a touch after pitching. Laura is early into her shot and ends up chipping it on the bounce to mid off.
Wide outside off, placed to point.
Served around off, spinning away, punched off the back foot to Knight at short cover.
ALEX HARTLEY comes on to bowl her left-arm spin. Surprising to see England not attacking. Might do with a slip in place.
Slower through the air outside off, pushed through the gap in covers for a single.
Sliding into the pads, worked behind square on the leg side for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Served fuller outside off, spinning in. Laura plays a punchy drive through covers. Winfield at sweeper cover, hares to her right and concedes just a single.
Spinning into the batsman, driven to mid on.
Laura punches it on the up in the cover region. Heather Knight at short extra cover, dives to her left and makes a good stop.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Shortish delivery around off, bounces a touch extra as well, run down to third man for a single.
Fuller length outside off, Wolvaardt leans ahead and block it.
Full outside off, driven to point.

FOUR! Wolvaardt makes full use of the width! Sciver drags her length a touch back and gives width too. Wolvaardt, who is out there for quite a time now, goes back and punches it past backward point. Beats the diving third man fielder and gets a boundary. A much-needed one for the Proteas! 50-up for South Africa as well!
Angling into the batsman, driven off the inner half to mid on.
Full outside off, Laura bends her knee and drives it through covers for a single. She will retain the strike.
Slightly on a shorter length, punched to short extra cover.
Slower through the air outside off, pushed to mid off.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Off spinner outside off, defended off the front foot on the off side.
Served fuller outside off, driven off the front foot to covers.
Again it's full outside off, driven off the outer half to point.
Full outside off, pushed to covers.
MIGNON DU PREEZ walks in at number 4, replacing Chetty.

OUT! EXCELLENT WORK FROM SARAH TAYLOR! Sciver slips it down the leg side. Chetty comes forward to flick it away but misses it completely. Taylor behind the stumps is super quick. Collects the ball and whips the bails off in a flash. The umpire goes upstairs to check it as Taylor has lost the ball in the process. After having a hard look at it, third umpire rules it in the favour of the fielding side. A wicket which belongs to Sarah Taylor. Wide is also signalled!
That is some work from Sarah Taylor! England are confident and the umpire has gone upstairs to refer a stumping appeal against Trisha Chetty.
Straighter one on a length around off, turned in the mid-wicket region. Both the batsmen take a start but then opt against it.
This time Laura flicks it away to fine leg for a single.
Angling into the pads, Wolvaardt looks to flick it away but misses and gets rapped on the pads.
Low full toss on middle and leg, driven to mid on.
Quicker through the air outside off, punched through covers for a single.

Flatter delivery wide outside off, Chetty runs it down past the keeper with a deft touch. Hartley from inside the circle gives it a chase and sweeps the ball in near the ropes. The umpire though has a check upstairs and confirms the clean stop. Three runs taken.
Tossed up outside off, Chetty pushes it off the front foot to mid off.
Spinning in from around off, clipped to square leg.
Full outside off, pushed through cover-point for a single.
Slower through the air outside off, steered behind point. Beaumont there, runs across to field and prevents the single.
End of the mandatory Powerplay. LAURA MARSH to start the proceedings after it. First sign of spin.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Outside off, Trisha looks to run it down to third man but is squared up by that late movement again. Is beaten.
Around off, watchfully defended.

FOUR! Edged away! This is one disadvantage with your keeper standing up. Sciver bowls a lovely delivery, landing it just outside off and then getting it to seam away. Chetty pushes at it but gets an outside edge. Luckily for her, it flies past Sarah Taylor standing up to the stumps and races away to the third man fence. Chetty moves to 12 with her second boundary.
Full and just outside off, watchfully defended by Trisha.
FOUR! Poor start. A half volley around middle and leg, Chetty covers the line well and flicks it to the mid-wicket fence.
First change. NATALIE SCIVER comes on to bowl medium pace. Sarah Taylor is up to the stumps.
Full and down the leg side, flicked towards square leg where Jenny Gunn misfields and concedes a single.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single. Shrubsole gets across from mid off and does well with a slide.
Played to the point region again.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Full and down the leg side, flicked a la flamingo style behind square leg for a single.
Slight change in the field. Lauren Winfield moves from first slip to gully. No slips now.
Outside off, steered to third man for a single.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Full and around off, pushed down the ground. Tammy Beaumont slides to her left from mid on and keeps the batters to a single.

FOUR! That is a good shot but a bit unlucky for Fran Wilson. Wolvaardt droves this beautifully through point and Wilson dived to her right to stop it. But unluckily for her, the ball bounced on one of the pitches and went well over her to the fence.

Today is Nelson Mandela day, observed in remembrance of the great soul. South Africa would dearly love to win today for him. Also, yesterday, the men had a tremendous victory in the second Test and the women would be looking to do something similar.
Outside off, steered behind point for a run.
A length ball outside off, Wolvaardt throws her bat at it and gets a thick outside edge to third man. A single taken.
A short ball, pulled through square leg. There is a misfield but mid-wicket mops it up. No run taken.
Full and around off, pushed towards cover.

Plenty of swing but there is no direction. The ball changes its direction from outside off towards leg and beats Chetty on her flick, hitting the pads. An LBW shout ensues but that was clearly going down the leg side.
A straight ball, on a length, watchfully blocked out.
Down the leg side, flicked away for a single.
Fuller length just outside off, swinging in, watchfully defended.
Full and wide outside off, driven beautifully but straight to point.
Stays back in her crease and blocks.
Outside off, coming in, left alone.
TRISHA CHETTY is the new woman in.

OUT! BOWLED! Shrubsole has her wicket eventually. No review needed here. A bit of a wild stroke from Lee though. It was on a length outside off and Lee swung wildly, perhaps a tad early. She missed and heard a sound which she would not have liked to hear. The ball hitting the off stump. Shrubsole roars in delight. That is a big, big wicket.
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
FOUR! Nicely done. Short and outside off, Lee goes back and cuts it nicely past a diving point to the fence.
A nice yorker on middle and off, well dug out.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Driven through the covers by the batsman.
Alan Wilkins on air mentioned earlier about Shrubsole's lethal inswinger. And that's what almost got the better of the dangerous Lizelle Lee in the previous over.
Outside off, played straight to point.

FOUR! Not quite where she intended to hit. On a length outside off, Wolvaardt looked to punch it through the covers but the late movement of the ball took the outside edge past first slip to third man fence.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. MAIDEN FROM SHRUBSOLE!

NOT OUT. The decision is overturned! What a review from Lee. Normally when you are given out, you are advised to think twice before taking the review if there is no wood involved. Lee obviously knew what she was doing. This was full and swinging in, Lee missed her flick and got pinged on her pads. There was a loud appeal and umpire Gregory Brathwaite raised his finger after a thought. Lee did not have a big chat with her partner, albeit straightaway signalled for the review. Hawk Eye showed that to be missing leg stump! Indeed, she was way too far down the track and perhaps that's what convinced her to go for the review.
Lizelle Lee has been adjudged lbw. She has taken the review immediately. She is way ahead of the crease and that can save her.
Nicely bowled, getting it to swing in the air and come into the batter, Lizelle defends watchfully.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Slips this down the leg side, Lee misses her flick. Strangely, no wide signalled.
Full and outside off, coming in slightly, pushed towards mid on.
Very well bowled. On a length outside off, Laura looks to punch it through the off side but is beaten.
Around off and middle, watchfully defended.
Short and outside off, pretty wide, cut through point but it is well fielded with a dive by Wilson again.
Outside off, just short of a length, Wolvaardt punches it through cover-point. But Fran Wilson gives it a good chase from point and saves the boundary. Two runs taken.
Flicks it through the leg side for a single. Played that very late. Much better placement from Lee.
Full and just outside off, watchfully pushed back towards mid on.
Once again movement takes the ball down the leg side from well outside off, LW misses her flick and is hit on the pads. An LBW shout is turned down.
On middle, pushed straight to mid on.
Comes back in a long way from outside off but slides down the leg side, Wolvaardt misses her flick. The ball goes off the pads towards fine leg but the keeper dives to her left to stop that.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
On a length outside off, pushed straight to cover.

TOP EDGE, SAFE! It is sliding down the leg side, would have been called a wide but Lee looks to sweep. However, she is a bit early and gets a top edge. It swirls in the air but does not carry to fine leg. A single taken.
ODINE KIRSTEN to bowl from the other end.
Slightly short outside off, Lizelle runs it down to third man for a single. Very good opening over for the Proteas.
WIDE. Full and down the leg side, Lee looks to sweep but misses.

Oohhh... holding the ball cross-seam, Brunt bowls it full and around off, Wolvaardt brings her bat down at the last moment to get an inside edge to fine leg. A single results. Had she been a second late, well, it would have been curtains - LBW or bowled.
Holds the length back a touch, LW goes back and runs it off the outer half of the bat behind point for a couple.
Outside off, nicely played towards cover.
A length ball down the leg side, Laura misses out on her flick, getting hit on the pads. There is an LBW shout but it was going down the leg side.
Uh oh.... Brunt comes running in but loses her runup. Is she nervous?
FOUR! What a way to start! A juicy full toss on the pads, but look at the audacity with which it is played! Wolvaardt gets down and sweeps it through backward square leg for a boundary!

The anthems are done and dusted. The English team gets into a huddle. The whole unit looks pumped up and there is a good feeling in this camp. Out come the South African openers, Laura Wolvaardt and Lizelle Lee. KATHERINE BRUNT to start off proceedings to Wolvaardt. Here we go!
Time for the national anthems. The South African one will be played first up.

Sanjay Manjrekar inspecting the pitch says that we are back at Bristol and back to brown and dry pitches. However, he feels today's pitch is less dry and rough than the English-West Indies game. Reckons that spinners will come into play and will rule while any seamer who is willing to take the pace off and bowl those cutters will get some purchase off the surface.

Heather Knight says that she was going to bat first as well. Hopes to make good use of the conditions now and the track first up and bowl well. Says that she has asked her team to be as relaxed as possible and hopes to put in another strong performance. Admits that England are still searching for their 'A' game as they have been scrapping a couple of wins in the recent past. Hopes that their 'A' performance comes in today. Says that England are unchanged from the previous game.

Van Niekerk wants to rectify the mistakes made in their previous game. Agrees that England are a world-class side and they need to be at their best to beat the hosts today. Informs that they have made one change, with CHLOE TRYON coming in for Masabata Klaas.
It is time for the spin of the coin. The captains are out in the middle and Protea skipper DANE VAN NIEKERK calls Tails. It is tails. SOUTH AFRICA CHOOSE TO BAT.

England are on a 6-match winning streak and 3 of those wins have been at Bristol. They were beaten by India in the opening game of this World Cup but since then they have come back roaring. South Africa have been up and down in this tournament but they will know that if they put two excellent performances in a row, they could hold the trophy in their hands, something which their male counterparts have struggled to do.

It is semi-final day! Forget the league games. 8 teams started the tournament and are now down to the final four. England and South Africa will play the first semi-final today while Australia and India battle it out on Thursday. Which will become the first team to enter the final? Stay tuned to find out!
